_readme: Settings of the network map. They describe which programs and adapters the map recognises. Edit freely without touching the code; restart the map after editing.

adapterKinds - the list of network adapter kinds. It is checked top to bottom and the first match wins (that is why NetBird is above the generic WireGuard). An adapter that matches no kind is treated as physical (real hardware) or other.

kind  - internal name. happ, clash, anyconnect, tailscale, netbird are reserved: they have their own data collectors (processes, settings files, console clients). Any other name is a generic kind: the map shows the adapter, its routes and a destination node, but no data from the program.
label - the caption on the map and in the legend. color - the colour.
nameRx / descRx - regular expressions (case-insensitive) for the Windows adapter name and description. One of the two is enough.
tun   - true if the program intercepts all traffic (a TUN VPN). It affects the findings about two TUNs at once and hijacked DNS.
vpn   - true to show the adapter even while it is down.
Paths may contain environment variables such as %APPDATA%.

processes._comment: Regular expressions for the process name (without .exe). proxyRx - programs that listen on a local proxy port (the 'Proxy 127.0.0.1:port' nodes are built from them).

paths._comment: Where to look for settings and console clients. If a file is missing, the corresponding block of the map is simply empty.
anyconnectCli: C:\Program Files*\Cisco\Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client\vpncli.exe

probes._comment: internetIp - the address used to find the 'to the internet' route. controlZone - the name for resolver probes. exitUrl - a page that returns the external IP (Cloudflare trace format).
